correctness.rationale: Equations (7)–(8) of arXiv:2604.10995v1 reduce exactly to the polynomial two-dimensional ODE in RESULT.md. The disease-free equilibrium is a saddle. A global positive derivative bound \(15185/28800>0\) for the endemic nullcline equation forces uniqueness; the sole endemic equilibrium is the exact repelling focus \((43/480,1/4)\), with trace \(8387/52440>0\), determinant \(1075/6992>0\), and negative characteristic discriminant. The exact inequality \(g(0,B)\le -B/20\) and the logarithmic \(L=I e^{-30B}\) argument give strict positive infectious and behaviour barriers. The physical square is forward invariant, and both upper faces are strictly inward pointing; every interior trajectory is therefore precompact in the open square. Since the unique interior equilibrium is a hyperbolic repeller, Poincaré–Bendixson proves periodic omega-limits for all other positive trajectories. All rational equalities were replayed using included verify.py and returned VERIFY_OK; no independent audit was conducted. Continuity justifies a nonempty \(q_c<1\) perturbation interval; no cycle period or uniqueness is claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 article gives an equilibrium-based phase portrait and public parameter set; whether its new quadratic behavioral coupling admits undriven epidemic waves is a natural missing dynamical classification. This theorem establishes an autonomous periodic regime at exact physically allowed positive parameters, proves persistent nonvanishing infection for all interior non-equilibrium initial states, and extends qualitatively to \(q_c<1\). It identifies a model-relevant qualitative boundary, not a textbook fixed-point deduction or an arbitrary finite statistic. General epidemic oscillations were known and are not claimed as new.
